items.title: Numerical reasoning: successive and reverse percentages (level 4)
items.source: Civil Service Jobs and GOV.UK: Civil Service online tests, practice guidance
items.body: At level 4 you meet percentages in sequence. The key idea is that each percentage applies to the amount you have at that point, not to the original. A 20% reduction followed by a further 10% reduction is not a 30% reduction. Work it in two steps: £50 less 20% is £40, and £40 less 10% is £36. The multiplier method is faster: multiply by 0.8 and then by 0.9. In the same way, a rise of 25% followed by a fall of 25% does not return you to the start. £80 rises to £100, and 25% of £100 is £25, leaving £75. To undo a percentage change, divide by the multiplier. If a salary after a 20% rise is £30,000, divide by 1.2 to get the original, £25,000. Do not take 20% off £30,000, because the 20% was a share of the original and not of the new figure. Repeated growth works the same way: 5% a year for two years is a multiplier of 1.05 twice. The order of percentage multipliers does not change the final result. A profit percentage is the profit divided by the cost, not by the selling price. Write the multiplier beside each step, and check that your answer is sensible.

questions.prompt: A £50 coat is reduced by 20% and then reduced by a further 10% of the new price. What is the final price?
The price of an item is £80. It rises by 25% and then falls by 25%. What is the final price?
After a 20% pay rise, an employee's salary is £30,000. What was the salary before the rise?
questions.hint: Divide by the multiplier: £30,000 ÷ 1.2 = £25,000.

questions.prompt: A team of 250 loses 8% of its staff and then recruits 35 new people. How many people are in the team afterwards?
An item costs £120 before VAT. VAT of 20% is added and then a 10% staff discount is taken off the total. What is the final price?
A population of 40,000 grows by 5% in each of two years. What is the population after two years?
A learner answers 36 of 48 questions correctly. What percentage is correct?
Goods cost a shop £800 and are sold for £1,000. What is the profit as a percentage of the cost?
questions.hint: Profit is £200; 200 ÷ 800 = 0.25, which is 25%.

items.title: Numerical reasoning: averages, ratios and rates with several steps (level 4)
items.source: Civil Service Jobs and GOV.UK: Civil Service online tests, practice guidance
items.body: Multi-step averages need you to move between means and totals. The total equals the mean multiplied by the number of values. If one value is removed, subtract it from the total and divide by one fewer value. If a new value is added and the mean changes, work out the old and new totals; their difference is the new value. Worked example: the mean of four values is 18, so the total is 72. After a fifth value is added the mean is 20, so the total is 100, and the fifth value is 28. A weighted mean takes account of group sizes: ten staff on £20,000 and five on £32,000 have a total pay of £360,000 across 15 staff, so the mean is £24,000. This is not the same as the mean of 20,000 and 32,000. Average speed is total distance divided by total time, not the mean of the speeds. Sixty miles at 30 mph takes 2 hours and 60 miles at 60 mph takes 1 hour, so 120 miles takes 3 hours, which is 40 mph. For a three-part ratio, add all the parts first. For the median of an odd number of values, sort them first, then take the middle one.

questions.prompt: The mean of six numbers is 25. One of the numbers, 40, is removed. What is the mean of the remaining five?
£500 is shared in the ratio 2:3:5. How much more does the largest share receive than the smallest share?
questions.hint: One part is £50; largest £250, smallest £100; difference £150.

questions.prompt: A cleaning concentrate is mixed with water in the ratio 1:9. How much mixture is made from 5 litres of concentrate?

options.text: 45 litres
46 litres
10 litres
50 litres

questions.hint: 1 part is 5 litres, so 10 parts make 50 litres.

questions.prompt: Ten staff earn £20,000 each and five staff earn £32,000 each. What is the mean salary of all fifteen?
What is the median of 12, 5, 9, 21, 7, 14 and 3?
questions.hint: In order: 3, 5, 7, 9, 12, 14, 21; the middle (fourth) value is 9.

questions.prompt: A van drives 60 miles at 30 mph and then another 60 miles at 60 mph. What is its average speed for the whole journey?

options.text: 45 mph
60 mph
40 mph
30 mph

questions.hint: Time is 2 + 1 = 3 hours; 120 ÷ 3 = 40 mph.

questions.prompt: The mean of four values is 18. When a fifth value is added, the mean becomes 20. What is the fifth value?
questions.hint: New total 100 minus old total 72 = 28.

questions.prompt: A recipe for 4 people uses 600 g of rice. How much rice is needed for 10 people?

items.title: Numerical reasoning: tax, interest and budgets (level 4)
items.source: Civil Service Jobs and GOV.UK: Civil Service online tests, practice guidance
items.body: Questions about budgets, tax and interest usually take three or four steps. Slow down and set each one out. Simple interest is calculated on the original amount only: 5% a year on £2,000 is £100 each year, so after 3 years the interest is £300. Tax is often charged only on income above an allowance. A salary of £30,000 with a £12,000 allowance has £18,000 taxable, and 20% of that is £3,600. Do not take 20% of the whole salary. When a charge includes VAT, work out the pre-VAT total first and then add 20%: hire at £45 an hour for 3.5 hours is £157.50, and VAT of £31.50 makes £189. To compare two ways of paying, calculate each total and subtract. A pass at £48 a month against 22 single trips at £2.40 (£52.80) saves £4.80. For budgets, add the shares that are already used and subtract from 100% before converting to money. A deduction such as a pension contribution is a percentage taken from gross pay, so multiply gross pay by one minus the rate. Mileage claims multiply miles by the rate per mile. Always write down the answer to each step and watch the units.

questions.prompt: £2,000 is borrowed at 5% simple interest a year for 3 years. How much interest is paid altogether?
A worker earns £30,000 a year. The first £12,000 is tax-free and the rest is taxed at 20%. How much tax is paid?
questions.hint: Taxable pay is £18,000; 20% of that is £3,600.

questions.prompt: A meeting room costs £45 an hour to hire. It is booked for 3.5 hours and 20% VAT is added. What is the total cost?
A monthly bus pass costs £48. A single trip costs £2.40 and Dev makes 22 trips in a month. How much does he save with the pass?
The rate is $1.25 to £1. Maya changes £450 into dollars and then spends $300. How many dollars does she have left?
A budget of £12,500 is split so that 40% goes on staff and 25% on premises. How much is left for other costs?
A mileage claim is paid at 45p a mile. How much is paid for a 86-mile journey?
An employee earns £15 an hour for 37.5 hours and pays 4% of gross pay into a pension. What is her pay after the pension payment?

items.title: Numerical reasoning: tables, charts and proportions (level 4)
items.source: Civil Service Jobs and GOV.UK: Civil Service online tests, practice guidance
items.body: In level 4 data questions, you are given a handful of figures and must pick the right operation. Start by writing down what each number stands for. Percentages from a table: divide the part by the total, then multiply by 100. If staff numbers by grade are AO 120, EO 80, HEO 40 and SEO 10, the total is 250 and AO staff are 120 ÷ 250 = 48%. A comparison 'how much more' as a percentage uses the smaller figure as the base: sales of 180 against 120 are 60 more, and 60 ÷ 120 = 50% more. To see which of two budgets was used up more, compare percentages, not pounds. A department that spent £150,000 of £200,000 used 75%, while one that spent £210,000 of £300,000 used 70%, even though it spent more money. A pie chart works with angles: 360 degrees is the whole, so if 90 degrees represent 45 staff, the whole is 180 staff and 150 degrees represents 75 staff. Time totals need care: add minutes first, then convert to hours. Question writers often include extra figures, so cross out what you do not need. Check your units: thousands in the table must be read as thousands in the answer.

questions.prompt: Staff numbers by grade are AO 120, EO 80, HEO 40 and SEO 10. What percentage of all staff are AO?
questions.hint: The total is 250; 120 ÷ 250 = 0.48, which is 48%.

questions.prompt: Sales in the South were £180,000 and in the North £120,000. By what percentage were South sales higher than North sales?
Complaints in January, February and March were 40, 52 and 46. What was the mean per month?
Department A has a budget of £200k and has spent £150k. Department B has a budget of £300k and has spent £210k. Which department has used the larger share of its budget?

options.text: Department B (70% used)
Department B (£210k spent)
Department A (75% used)
Department A (£50k left)

questions.prompt: Visitors on Monday to Friday were 120, 150, 90, 180 and 210. What percentage of the week's visitors came on Friday?
questions.hint: Total is 750; 210 ÷ 750 = 0.28, which is 28%.

questions.prompt: There were 800 cases in 2022 and 920 cases in 2023. What was the percentage increase?
questions.hint: The rise is 120; 120 ÷ 800 = 0.15, which is 15%.

questions.prompt: Three tasks take 25, 40 and 55 minutes. What is the total time in hours?

options.text: 1.5 hours
2.33 hours
1.2 hours
2 hours

questions.hint: 25 + 40 + 55 = 120 minutes, which is 2 hours.

questions.prompt: A pie chart shows that 90 degrees represent 45 staff. How many staff are represented by 150 degrees?
questions.hint: 1 degree = 0.5 staff, so 150 degrees = 75 staff.

items.title: Numerical reasoning: rates, time and work (level 4)
items.source: Civil Service Jobs and GOV.UK: Civil Service online tests, practice guidance
items.body: Rate questions describe work being done over time. The reliable method is to find the rate for one unit: one person, one hour or one litre. A team of 4 completes 120 forms in 3 hours, which is 10 forms per person per hour. For 6 people over 5 hours the total is 6 × 5 × 10 = 300. Where two rates act at once, such as a tank that fills and drains, subtract to get the net rate. Filling at 25 litres a minute and draining at 10 litres a minute gives a net 15 litres a minute, and 600 litres takes 40 minutes. For speed, distance and time, convert times to hours. A journey from 12:15 to 14:45 lasts 2.5 hours, so at 72 mph the distance is 180 miles. Converting speeds: kilometres per hour divided by 3.6 gives metres per second, so 72 km/h is 20 m/s. Calendar questions need counting days: 19 days after Monday 1 March, remove sets of 7 and count what remains. Printing and charges often have a set-up cost plus a rate per batch. Make a short list: what is the rate, what is the quantity, what is added on. Finally, check that your answer is the right size.

questions.prompt: A team of 4 completes 120 forms in 3 hours. At the same rate, how many forms would 6 people complete in 5 hours?
questions.hint: 10 forms per person per hour; 6 × 5 × 10 = 300.

questions.prompt: A train travels from 12:15 to 14:45 at an average speed of 72 mph. How far does it travel?

options.text: 216 miles
180 miles
144 miles
162 miles

questions.hint: The journey is 2.5 hours; 72 × 2.5 = 180 miles.

questions.prompt: A tank is filled at 25 litres a minute while draining at 10 litres a minute. How long does it take to hold 600 litres?

options.text: 24 minutes
40 minutes
60 minutes
17.14 minutes

questions.hint: Net rate is 15 litres a minute; 600 ÷ 15 = 40 minutes.

questions.prompt: If 1 March is a Monday, what day of the week is 20 March?

options.text: Saturday
Friday
Sunday
Thursday

questions.hint: 19 days later: 19 = 2 weeks + 5 days; Monday + 5 days = Saturday.

questions.prompt: A speed of 72 km/h is the same as how many metres per second?

options.text: 72 m/s
20 m/s

questions.hint: Divide km/h by 3.6: 72 ÷ 3.6 = 20.

questions.prompt: A printer charges £12.50 per 100 leaflets plus a £5 set-up fee. What is the cost of 250 leaflets?
A report needs 90 hours of work. Five staff each work 6 hours a day on it. How many days does it take?

options.text: 18 days
15 days
3 days
30 days

questions.hint: 5 × 6 = 30 hours a day; 90 ÷ 30 = 3 days.

questions.prompt: Each box weighs 2.25 kg. A person can safely carry up to 30 kg. How many boxes can they carry in one trip?

options.text: 14 boxes
12 boxes
13 boxes
15 boxes

questions.hint: 30 ÷ 2.25 = 13.3, so 13 whole boxes.

items.title: Verbal reasoning: true, false or cannot say, data in text (level 4)
items.source: Civil Service Jobs and GOV.UK: Civil Service online tests, practice guidance
items.body: At level 4, passages often contain figures, and the statement may need a small calculation. Keep your method: use only the passage, find the evidence, and decide. When numbers are involved, do the arithmetic before you choose. Percentages in a passage refer to a particular group, so check which one. If '40% of applicants were women' and the total was 500, then 200 were women. A statement that says 'more than 150 women applied' is True, but a statement about how many women were successful is Cannot say unless the passage gives it. Be careful with relative words: 'twice as many' and 'twice as fast' need a clear comparison, and 'increase of 10 percentage points' differs from 'a 10% increase'. Also watch words such as 'approximately', 'at least' and 'no more than'. Worked example: 'Of 200 staff surveyed, 60% said they work from home at least one day a week.' The statement '120 staff work from home at least once a week' is True. The statement 'Most staff work from home every day' is Cannot say. The statement 'Fewer than half work from home' is False. Make sure you read the whole sentence before you calculate.

questions.prompt: "A recruitment campaign received 500 applications. Forty per cent of applicants were women. Of all the applicants, 50 were already civil servants." Statement: "More than 150 women applied." Based only on the passage, which option is correct?

options.text: False: 40% of 500 is only 150
True: 40% of 500 is 200, which is more than 150
Cannot say: the passage does not give the sex of each applicant
Cannot say: the passage does not say how many were successful

questions.prompt: "Of 200 staff surveyed, 60% said they work from home at least one day a week. The survey was carried out in January." Statement: "Fewer than half of the staff surveyed work from home at least one day a week." Using only the passage, which option is correct?

options.text: False: 60% is more than half
True: only some staff were surveyed
Cannot say: the passage does not name the staff
Cannot say: the survey may not cover all days

questions.hint: 60% of the 200 surveyed is 120, which is more than half.

questions.prompt: "The call centre answered 90% of calls within 30 seconds in April. In May the figure was 94%. In both months it received around 4,000 calls." Statement: "The number of calls answered within 30 seconds was higher in May than in April." Which option is correct, judged only on the passage?

options.text: True: 94% is higher than 90%
Cannot say: the call totals are only approximately equal
False: the number of calls was the same
False: the percentage of calls answered in time fell between the two months

questions.hint: With 'around 4,000' in both months, the exact numbers cannot be compared with certainty.

questions.prompt: "The unemployment rate fell from 5.5% to 4.5% over the year. The government described the fall as the largest in a decade." Statement: "The unemployment rate fell by one percentage point." Based only on the passage, which option is correct?

options.text: True: 5.5% minus 4.5% is 1 percentage point
False: it fell by 1%, which is a different amount
Cannot say: the passage does not give the number of people
Cannot say: the passage does not say which year it was

questions.hint: 5.5 − 4.5 = 1 percentage point.

questions.prompt: "Staff may claim up to £80 a night for hotel stays outside London and up to £120 a night in London. Claims above these limits need written approval." Statement: "A claim for £100 a night in Manchester needs written approval." Using only the passage, which option is correct?

options.text: False: £100 is below the London limit
True: the limit outside London is £80
Cannot say: the passage does not say if Manchester is in London
Cannot say: the passage does not give the length of stay

questions.hint: Manchester is outside London, where £100 exceeds the £80 limit.

questions.prompt: "Twice as many people used the online service in June as in May. In May, 3,000 people used it. The telephone service was used by 5,000 people in June." Statement: "More people used the online service than the telephone service in June." Which option is correct, judged only on the passage?

options.text: False: the telephone service had 5,000 users
True: online use was 6,000, which is more than 5,000
Cannot say: the telephone figure for May is not given
Cannot say: online use may be different in July

questions.hint: 2 × 3,000 = 6,000, which is higher than 5,000.

questions.prompt: "The department aims to reduce its energy use by 15% by 2030 compared with 2020. In 2020 it used 2 million units of energy." Statement: "By 2030 the department aims to use no more than 1.7 million units." Based only on the passage, which option is correct?

options.text: False: the department aims to use 1.85 million units
Cannot say: the passage does not state what the target for 2030 actually is
Cannot say: the passage does not say what a unit is
True: 15% of 2 million is 300,000, leaving 1.7 million

questions.prompt: "The audit examined 120 case files and found errors in 18 of them. The auditors recommended extra training for staff." Statement: "The errors were caused by a lack of training." Using only the passage, which option is correct?

options.text: True: the auditors recommended extra training
Cannot say: the passage recommends training but gives no cause
False: the errors were caused by faulty systems and out-of-date software
False: only a few files contained errors

questions.hint: A recommendation does not prove the cause of the errors.

items.title: Verbal reasoning: true, false or cannot say, organisations and rules (level 4)
items.source: Civil Service Jobs and GOV.UK: Civil Service online tests, practice guidance
items.body: These passages describe how organisations or rules work, and the statements test whether you can apply the rule or spot what is missing. Read the passage in layers. First, find the main rule. Next, look for exceptions, introduced by words such as 'unless', 'except', 'however' and 'but'. Finally, note any conditions about who, when and how much. A statement is True if the rule and its conditions clearly lead to it. It is False if the rule or an exception clearly leads to the opposite. It is Cannot say if you would need extra facts. Worked example: 'Staff may work from home on up to two days a week, unless they are in their first three months.' For a person with six months' service, working from home on two days is True. For a person in month two, working from home on one day is False, because the exception applies. Whether a person with six months' service can work from home on three days is False. Whether the person works from home on Mondays is Cannot say. Mark the exceptions with a pencil, and always apply them before you decide.

questions.prompt: "Staff may work from home on up to two days a week, unless they are in their first three months. Managers must approve a home-working pattern in advance." Statement: "A member of staff in their second month can work from home one day a week." Which option is correct, judged only on the passage?

options.text: False: staff in their first three months are excluded
True: staff can work from home up to two days
Cannot say: the passage does not say how long the pattern lasts
Cannot say: the passage does not say if managers approve

questions.hint: The 'unless' clause excludes someone in their second month.

questions.prompt: "Grant applications are scored out of 100. Applications scoring 70 or more are funded, unless the budget has run out, in which case they are placed on a waiting list." Statement: "An application scoring 75 is certain to be funded." Based only on the passage, which option is correct?

options.text: True: scores of 70 or more are funded
False: it may go on the waiting list if the budget is spent
Cannot say: the passage does not say how large the grant budget actually is
Cannot say: the passage does not give the pass mark

questions.hint: The budget exception means a high score does not guarantee funding.

questions.prompt: "All contractors must hold a valid pass. Passes are issued by the security office on weekdays only. Emergency repairs are exempt from this requirement." Statement: "A contractor doing an emergency repair at the weekend must have a valid pass." Using only the passage, which option is correct?

options.text: True: all contractors must hold a valid pass
Cannot say: the passage does not say who gives the pass at weekends
False: emergency repairs are exempt
Cannot say: the passage does not define an emergency

questions.hint: The exemption removes the requirement for emergency repairs.

questions.prompt: "The complaints team aims to reply to every complaint within 10 working days. Complex cases that need an investigation may take up to 30 working days." Statement: "A complex complaint may take 25 working days to answer." Which option is correct, judged only on the passage?

options.text: True: complex cases may take up to 30 working days
False: every complaint is answered within 10 days
Cannot say: the passage does not say how complex cases are defined
Cannot say: the passage does not say how many complaints there are

questions.hint: 25 days is within the 30-day limit for complex cases.

questions.prompt: "Each directorate has its own training budget. A directorate that underspends in one year may carry up to 10% of its budget into the next year." Statement: "A directorate can carry its whole unspent budget into the next year." Based only on the passage, which option is correct?

options.text: False: the carry-over is limited to 10% of the budget
True: unspent money can be carried over
Cannot say: the passage does not say how much each directorate has
Cannot say: the passage does not say what training is

questions.hint: Only up to 10% can be carried over.

questions.prompt: "Interviews for the post will be held in London. Candidates travelling more than 100 miles can claim standard-class rail fares. Hotel costs are not covered." Statement: "A candidate living 60 miles away can claim a rail fare." Using only the passage, which option is correct?

options.text: True: candidates can claim rail fares
False: candidates cannot claim any fares
False: only hotel costs can be claimed
Cannot say: the passage gives the rule only for journeys over 100 miles

questions.hint: The rule says nothing about shorter journeys.

questions.prompt: "The online form saves progress automatically for 14 days. After that, any unsent form is deleted. Users who register an account can request one extension of seven days." Statement: "A registered user can keep an unsent form for up to 21 days." Which option is correct, judged only on the passage?

options.text: True: 14 days plus a seven-day extension is 21 days
False: the form is deleted after 14 days for everybody
Cannot say: the passage does not say how to register
Cannot say: the passage does not say if progress is saved

questions.prompt: "New starters shadow an experienced colleague for their first two weeks. During this time they do not handle customer calls on their own." Statement: "New starters take customer calls alone in their third week." Based only on the passage, which option is correct?

options.text: True: the shadowing ends after two weeks
False: they never take calls alone
Cannot say: the passage covers only the first two weeks
False: they shadow a colleague for the whole of their first month

questions.hint: What happens after the first two weeks is not stated.

items.title: Verbal reasoning: the best summary or conclusion (level 4)
items.source: Civil Service Jobs and GOV.UK: Civil Service online tests, practice guidance
items.body: Longer passages may be followed by a question such as 'Which of the following best summarises the passage?' or 'Which conclusion is best supported?'. A good summary covers the main point and does not add anything new. A weak summary can be too narrow, focusing on a single detail, or too broad, claiming more than the passage says. It may also distort the meaning with stronger words. Method: after reading, write one sentence of your own about what the passage is saying. Then compare each option with your sentence. Remove options that include information not in the passage. Remove options that give only one example. Remove options that overstate. Worked example: 'The agency has cut waiting times by 20% over two years. It credits a new booking system and extra weekend appointments, although some centres still report long delays.' A good summary is: waiting times have fallen, though not at every centre. Too narrow: the agency has a new booking system. Too broad: all waiting times have been solved. Distorted: weekend appointments are the only reason for the fall. When two options both look right, choose the one that includes the 'although' or 'but' idea if the passage includes it.

questions.prompt: The agency has cut waiting times by 20% over two years. It credits a new booking system and extra weekend appointments, although some centres still report long delays. Which option best summarises the passage?

options.text: The new booking system has solved the problem of long waiting times at every centre
Waiting times have fallen overall, but some centres still have long delays
Weekend appointments are the only reason waiting times have fallen
The agency now has fewer centres than it did two years ago

questions.hint: The summary must include both the fall and the remaining problem.

questions.prompt: Many offices are moving to hybrid working. Surveys show that staff value flexibility, but some managers worry about team spirit. Training in remote management is being introduced. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: Staff are against hybrid working because it harms team spirit
Hybrid working brings benefits and concerns, and support is being offered to managers
Remote management training will make all managers support hybrid working across the department
Hybrid working has been shown to cut costs in all offices

questions.hint: The passage is balanced and mentions training being introduced.

questions.prompt: The museum's visitor numbers rose by 12% after it introduced free entry, although income from ticket sales fell. The museum says donations have partly made up the difference. Which option best summarises the passage?

options.text: Free entry increased visitors but reduced ticket income, which donations partly replaced
Free entry has made the museum more successful financially
Donations are now the museum's main source of income
Visitors prefer museums that do not charge for tickets

questions.hint: The summary needs the rise in visitors, the loss of ticket income, and the partial offset.

questions.prompt: A report on road safety notes that accidents fell by 8% in areas with new speed cameras. However, it adds that the cameras were installed at the most dangerous sites, so other factors may be involved. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: Speed cameras are the most effective way of cutting accidents
Accidents increased in areas without speed cameras
Accidents fell where cameras were installed, but the cameras may not be the only reason
Cameras should be installed everywhere without delay

questions.hint: The report is cautious about cause.

questions.prompt: The council plans to close two small libraries and open one larger library in the town centre. It says this will save money and offer longer opening hours. Local residents have raised concerns about travel. Which option best summarises the passage?

options.text: Residents have forced the council to cancel its plans
The council plans a change in libraries that it says will save money, though residents are concerned
The new library will be cheaper to visit than the old ones
The council is closing all the libraries in the town

questions.hint: The summary needs the plan, the council's reasons and the residents' concern.

questions.prompt: A study of 1,000 employees found that those who took regular breaks reported lower stress. The authors note that the study cannot show whether breaks are the cause. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: Taking regular breaks removes stress at work
Regular breaks are linked to lower stress, but a cause has not been shown
Employees who report low stress take more breaks
Stress is the cause of staff skipping breaks

questions.hint: The authors warn that a link is not proof of a cause.

questions.prompt: The helpline will move to a new phone number on 1 June. The old number will continue to work for six months, and callers will hear a message about the change. Which option best summarises the passage?

options.text: The helpline is changing its number, with the old number working for a time
The helpline will close on 1 June
Callers must use the new number straight away
The helpline will have longer opening hours

questions.hint: The summary captures both the change and the transition period.

questions.prompt: A department found that 70% of its forms were completed online and the rest on paper. Paper forms cost four times as much to process. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: Moving more forms online is likely to reduce processing costs
All paper forms will be abolished next year
Online forms are always more accurate than paper forms are in this department
Staff dislike processing paper forms

questions.hint: Paper forms cost more, so reducing them would probably cut costs.

items.title: Verbal reasoning: assumptions and what would weaken a claim (level 4)
items.source: Civil Service Jobs and GOV.UK: Civil Service online tests, practice guidance
items.body: Some questions ask you to think about the strength of an argument. An argument gives a reason and draws a conclusion, and it often depends on an unstated assumption. Example: 'Visitor numbers rose after the new signs were put up, so the signs worked.' This assumes that nothing else caused the rise. A statement that would weaken the claim is a fact that gives another explanation, such as 'A big event took place nearby that month'. A statement that would strengthen the claim shows that the reason is likely, such as 'Visitors said they found the museum by following the signs'. A statement that is irrelevant does nothing, for example 'The signs were blue'. Method: first, find the conclusion and the evidence. Then ask what must be true for the evidence to support the conclusion. Check each option for its effect. Weakening options introduce alternative causes or show the sample is small or unusual. Strengthening options rule out alternatives or add support. Choose the option that matches the question's wording, and read carefully whether it asks for strengthening or weakening.

questions.prompt: Visitor numbers rose after new signs were put up, so the signs must have worked. Which statement would most weaken this claim?

options.text: The signs were painted blue and white
The signs cost £500 to make
Visitors said that the museum looked very clean and welcoming
A large public event took place nearby that month

questions.hint: A nearby event gives another explanation for the rise.

questions.prompt: Staff morale improved after the office was repainted, so repainting improves morale. Which statement would most strengthen this claim?

options.text: The office was repainted in the summer
Staff said that the new colours made them feel happier at work
The paint was supplied by a local firm
Morale surveys are carried out in the office at the end of each year

questions.hint: Staff attributing the change to the paint supports the claim.

questions.prompt: Complaints fell by 30% after a new phone system was installed, so the system improved service. Which statement would most weaken this claim?

options.text: The new system was installed on a Monday
Staff were trained on the system for two days
The system came from a well-known supplier
The department stopped recording some types of complaint in the same month

questions.hint: A change in recording could explain the fall without better service.

questions.prompt: A town has more cafes than it did five years ago, so more people must be visiting the town. What does this argument assume?

options.text: Cafes open where there are more customers
Cafes in the town charge low prices
Most visitors prefer coffee to tea
The town centre has recently been redeveloped to attract firms

questions.hint: The conclusion depends on cafes opening in response to demand.

questions.prompt: Employees who attend the optional fitness class take fewer sick days, so the class improves health. Which statement would most weaken this claim?

options.text: Only employees who are already very healthy choose to attend the class
The class is held at lunchtime
The class has been running for two years
The teacher is a qualified instructor

questions.hint: Healthy people choosing the class explains the pattern without the class causing it.

questions.prompt: Applications rose after the job advert was rewritten in plain English. The department concludes that plain English attracts more applicants. Which statement would most strengthen this?

options.text: The advert was also published on a Monday
The job pays a competitive salary
The department received 400 applications
Applicants reported that the clearer wording made the role easier to understand

questions.hint: Applicants' own reports link the wording to the decision to apply.

questions.prompt: The new bus timetable was introduced and passenger numbers fell, so the timetable is the cause. What does this argument assume?

options.text: Most passengers read the new timetable carefully before travelling
The buses were running on time
Nothing else changed that would reduce passenger numbers
The new timetable is easier to print

questions.hint: The argument assumes no other cause for the fall.

questions.prompt: A report says that schools with longer lunch breaks have better exam results, and suggests extending lunch breaks everywhere. Which statement would most weaken the suggestion?

options.text: Lunch breaks are popular with pupils
The report was written by an educational charity
Most schools have a canteen
Schools with longer breaks also tend to be in wealthier areas with extra resources

questions.hint: Wealth and resources could explain the better results.

items.title: Verbal reasoning: ordering and sequence puzzles (level 4)
items.source: Civil Service Jobs and GOV.UK: Civil Service online tests, practice guidance
items.body: Some verbal reasoning questions give you facts about the order of things: who finished first, which file is on top, which step comes next. They are really short logic puzzles, and the way to solve them is to build a line. Put the first fact on your scrap paper, then add each new fact in the right place. For example: 'Anna finished before Ben. Ben finished before Carla.' This gives the line Anna, Ben, Carla, so Carla was last. Do not skip a fact, and do not assume something the text does not say. When a fact only fixes the order of two items, such as 'E is below A', leave space for others until further facts place them. For days of the week, count carefully and keep in mind which days are working days. If the training is the day before a Wednesday launch, it is on Tuesday, and an audit two days after the training is on Thursday. For positions in a row, test the possibilities. If two people must sit next to each other, treat them as a pair and see where the pair can fit. When all the facts are placed, read the line back against each statement in the passage to check it. If a question asks what must be true, pick the option that holds in every possible arrangement.

questions.prompt: Anna finished the task before Ben. Ben finished before Carla. Who finished last?

options.text: Anna
Ben
It cannot be worked out from the facts
Carla

questions.hint: The order is Anna, Ben, Carla.

questions.prompt: Five files are stacked. File B is above D. D is above A. C is above B. E is below A. Which file is on top?

options.text: File B
File D
File C
File A

questions.hint: The stack from top is C, B, D, A, E.

questions.prompt: A system launch is on Wednesday. Staff training is the day before the launch. The audit is two days after the training. On which day is the audit?

options.text: Wednesday
Thursday
Friday
Tuesday

questions.hint: Training is Tuesday; two days later is Thursday.

questions.prompt: Dev, Eve, Fay and Gus sit at desks 1 to 4 in a row. Dev is at desk 1. Eve sits next to Fay. Dev does not sit next to Gus. Who sits at desk 4?

options.text: Eve
Fay
Dev
Gus

questions.hint: Gus cannot be at 2, and Eve and Fay need two adjacent desks, so Gus is at desk 4.

questions.prompt: Tom is taller than Una. Una is taller than Val. Wes is shorter than Val. Which statement must be true?

options.text: Una is shorter than Wes
Tom is taller than Wes
Val is the shortest of the four
Wes is taller than Una

questions.hint: The order is Tom, Una, Val, Wes, so Tom is taller than Wes.

questions.prompt: The red report is longer than the green report. The blue report is shorter than the green report. Which report is the shortest?

options.text: The red report
The blue report
The green report
The red and blue reports are the same length

questions.hint: The order is red, green, blue from longest to shortest.

questions.prompt: The manager reviews the list every Monday. The list must be updated two working days before the review. The review is on Monday 14th. On which day is the list updated?

options.text: Friday 11th
Wednesday 9th
Sunday 13th
Thursday 10th

questions.hint: Two working days before Monday are Friday and Thursday, so Thursday.

questions.prompt: A form passes through five steps: scan, check, approve, file and notify. Check is always after scan. Approve is after check. File only happens after approve. Notify is always last. Which step is third?

options.text: Check
File
Approve
Scan

questions.hint: The order is scan, check, approve, file, notify.

items.title: Situational judgement: competing demands from managers and customers (level 4)
items.source: GOV.UK: The Civil Service Code and Civil Service Jobs candidate guidance
items.body: Real jobs rarely give you one problem at a time. At level 4, situational judgement questions place two reasonable demands on you, and several options may seem sensible. To pick the best, work out what is most urgent, who is affected and what the rules require. Then look for the response that deals with the pressing issue while keeping everyone informed. Good responses usually involve a quick, open conversation with the person who has the authority to decide, such as your manager. They avoid dropping a customer without explanation, and they avoid promising what you cannot deliver. Worked example: a customer arrives in person with an urgent query while your manager has asked for a spreadsheet by the end of the hour. A strong response is to deal with the customer if it can be done quickly or arrange for a colleague to help, then let your manager know that the spreadsheet may be a few minutes late and why. A weaker response is to ignore the customer to meet the deadline, or to forget the spreadsheet without telling your manager. Before you choose, ask: who needs to know, and what harm could result if I do nothing?

questions.prompt: A customer arrives in person with an urgent query while your manager has asked for a spreadsheet within the hour. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Ask the customer to wait without telling them how long it will take
Finish the spreadsheet first and then tell your manager you were busy
Tell your manager that you cannot do the spreadsheet because of customers
Help the customer or arrange cover, then tell your manager the spreadsheet may be slightly late and why

questions.hint: Dealing with the customer and keeping your manager informed handles both demands.

questions.prompt: Two managers give you different tasks and each says theirs is the priority. Both are due today. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Choose the task for the manager you work with most often
Do half of each task so that both of the managers see that work has started
Explain the situation to both managers and ask them to agree the priority
Do the easiest task first and tell neither manager

questions.hint: Asking the managers to agree puts the decision with those who can make it.

questions.prompt: A customer asks you to bend a rule because they are in a hurry. You have the power to do it but it would be unfair to others. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Make an exception, since it will only affect one case
Explain politely that you must treat everyone the same and describe the options open to them
Make the exception and ask the customer not to mention it
Refuse to speak to the customer any longer

questions.hint: Applying rules fairly and explaining options is consistent and respectful.

questions.prompt: You have promised a customer a call back at 3pm but your manager calls an urgent meeting at the same time. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Skip the call and hope the customer does not mind
Leave the meeting without explanation to make the call
Ring the customer at 5pm without telling them why
Ask a colleague to ring the customer or ring them to rearrange before the meeting

questions.hint: Keeping the customer informed and arranging cover maintains trust.

questions.prompt: Your manager asks you to finish a task by 5pm, but a system outage means that you cannot complete it. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Tell your manager now about the outage and agree what to do instead
Wait until 5pm and report that it is not finished
Complete a partial version of the task and report that it is completely finished
Ask a colleague to say it was done

questions.hint: Early notice lets your manager adjust plans.

questions.prompt: A senior officer from another team asks you to prioritise their request over your own team's task. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Say you will check with your manager, then confirm what is possible
Do their task at once, because they are senior
Refuse, because it is not your team's work
Do the task as asked but not mention it to your own manager until later

questions.hint: Your manager sets your priorities, so check with them.

questions.prompt: A customer is in the middle of a long call when your lunch break begins. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Hang up and go for lunch
Finish helping the customer if the call is close to being resolved, then take your break
Transfer the customer without explanation
Ask the customer to call back tomorrow

questions.hint: Completing a nearly finished call is helpful, and you can still take your break.

questions.prompt: You are asked to produce a report quickly and are tempted to use figures from an old source that you have not checked. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Check that the figures are current and tell the requester if you cannot confirm them in time
Use the figures and mention nothing
Leave out the figures to save time
Estimate the figures to look current

questions.hint: Accuracy matters more than speed, and the requester should know of limits.

items.title: Situational judgement: raising concerns and doing the right thing (level 4)
items.source: GOV.UK: The Civil Service Code and Civil Service Jobs candidate guidance
items.body: The Civil Service Code says that if you see something wrong, you should report it. This could be a safety risk, a possible fraud, bullying, or a breach of the rules. You do not need to be certain; you need to report it in good faith to your line manager, another manager or the Civil Service Commission if your own department cannot help. You should not ignore it, investigate on your own, or spread rumours. Situational judgement questions test whether you can balance loyalty to colleagues with your duty to report serious matters. Minor issues, such as a colleague forgetting to sign out, may be handled by a quiet word. Serious issues, such as fraud, safety risks or abuse of vulnerable people, should be reported to the proper person quickly. Worked example: you see a colleague changing customer bank details without authority. The most effective response is to report it to your manager or the fraud team straight away, and not to confront the colleague or wait to see if it happens again. Protect the evidence and keep what you know confidential.

questions.prompt: You see a colleague changing a customer's bank details without authority. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Confront the colleague and ask them to stop
Wait to see whether it happens again
Report it straight away to your manager or the fraud team
Mention it to other colleagues to see whether they noticed it too

questions.hint: Possible fraud is serious and must be reported through the proper channel.

questions.prompt: A colleague regularly forgets to log out of the system at the end of the day. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Report them to the director straight away
Remind them quietly and explain why it matters
Log in and make changes in their name as a joke
Ignore it, since it is minor

questions.hint: A quiet word is proportionate for a minor issue.

questions.prompt: You hear that a manager has been giving contracts to a company run by their brother. You have no proof. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Spread the story among your colleagues so that the truth will eventually emerge
Report your concern in good faith to a senior manager or the proper channel
Say nothing, as you have no proof
Confront the manager and demand an explanation

questions.hint: You can raise a concern in good faith without proof, and others will investigate.

questions.prompt: You discover that safety checks on the fire alarm have not been done this month, although the log says they have. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Correct the log so it shows the checks were done late, without telling anyone
Do the checks yourself without telling anyone
Report it to your manager or the health and safety officer immediately
Wait for the next scheduled audit

questions.hint: False records and missed safety checks are serious and should be reported promptly.

questions.prompt: A colleague tells you they have been bullied by a team member but ask you to keep it secret. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Promise to keep it secret and say nothing
Confront the team member yourself
Tell everyone in the team so that it stops
Listen, explain you may need to report it, and encourage them to speak to a manager

questions.hint: Bullying is serious; you can support them while making clear it should be reported.

questions.prompt: A temporary worker appears to be accessing files that are not part of their job. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Report what you saw to your manager or security without accusing the person
Tell the worker off in front of the team
Block their account yourself
Ignore it, as they are temporary

questions.hint: Reporting facts to the right person allows a proper investigation.

questions.prompt: You think that your manager has made an honest error that gives a customer too much money. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Quietly correct the amount in the system without telling your manager or anyone
Raise it politely with your manager and offer to check the figures with them
Let it go as it favours the customer
Tell the customer about the error before your manager

questions.hint: Raising it with your manager is open and gives them the chance to correct it.

questions.prompt: You are asked to delete an email that could show your department made a mistake. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Delete it, as your manager told you to
Move it to a folder where nobody will look
Forward it to your home email
Explain that you cannot delete records and speak to a senior manager

questions.hint: Records must be kept; if you are uncomfortable, raise it with a senior manager.

items.title: Situational judgement: pressure, wellbeing and professional behaviour (level 4)
items.source: GOV.UK: The Civil Service Code and Civil Service Jobs candidate guidance
items.body: Civil servants are expected to remain professional when under pressure and to look after their wellbeing so that they can do their job well. Situational judgement questions at this level include busy periods, tough conversations and the blurring of work and home life. Effective responses show self-awareness and communication. Tell your manager early if workload or stress is affecting you. Take breaks, use support such as employee assistance programmes, and use the proper channels. Avoid venting on social media, working in secret overtime that no one knows about, or letting stress affect how you treat customers. Professional behaviour also covers online conduct. The Civil Service Code requires you to be politically impartial in your work, and this applies to your posts online if they could be linked to your job. Worked example: after a difficult day you feel like posting a complaint about your department on social media. The best response is to take time to calm down and raise the issue with your manager. The next day you can discuss the problem with a clear head. Think about the effect on the public, on your team and on trust in the Civil Service.

questions.prompt: After a difficult day you want to post a complaint about your department on social media. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Take time to calm down and raise your concerns with your manager
Post it, but without naming the department
Post it in a private group of friends
Post it anonymously from a new account so it cannot be traced to you

questions.hint: Raising concerns internally protects trust and gets them dealt with.

questions.prompt: You have been working late for several weeks and feel exhausted. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Carry on and keep working late for the next few weeks to prove yourself
Talk to your manager about your workload and look at support available
Take sick leave without saying why
Do the minimum without telling anyone

questions.hint: Telling your manager early allows them to help before it affects your work.

questions.prompt: A customer has been very upset and you feel shaken after a call. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Take the next call straight away
Tell no one so you do not seem weak
Leave work for the day without telling anyone where you have gone or why
Take a short break and tell your manager or a colleague you trust

questions.hint: Taking a moment and seeking support is a sensible way to keep working well.

questions.prompt: A friend asks which political party your department supports. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Name the party you personally prefer
Explain that civil servants are politically impartial and serve whichever government is elected
Say that the department supports the governing party
Tell them politics is a secret

questions.hint: Civil servants serve governments of any party impartially.

questions.prompt: You are asked to work on a project that goes against your personal political views. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Refuse to work on it
Do a poor job to show your view
Tell the press what you think
Do the work professionally, because civil servants serve the government of the day

questions.hint: Impartiality means doing the work whatever your own opinions.

questions.prompt: A colleague sends you a joke by email that could offend some people. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Forward it to friends outside work
Reply with a bigger joke
Do not forward it and politely tell your colleague it may be inappropriate
Delete it and say nothing to your colleague, even though other people may also receive it

questions.hint: A polite word helps to keep the workplace respectful.

questions.prompt: Your workload doubles because a colleague is on leave. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Take on everything and work through lunch
Ignore the extra tasks until the colleague returns
Tell your manager and agree what to prioritise while the colleague is away
Ask the customers to wait

questions.hint: Agreeing priorities with your manager keeps the service running.

questions.prompt: At a social event a friend asks you about a confidential government project you work on. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Give a few details that do not seem sensitive to you
Hint at what you can and cannot say
Tell them where to find the information
Say that you are unable to discuss your work

questions.hint: Confidential information must not be shared outside work.

items.title: Situational judgement: using resources properly and avoiding conflicts of interest (level 4)
items.source: GOV.UK: The Civil Service Code and Civil Service Jobs candidate guidance
items.body: Civil servants use public money and public resources, and they must use them properly. The Civil Service Code requires integrity: you must not misuse your official position, use official resources for private gain, or let a personal interest affect your decisions. A conflict of interest arises when a personal relationship or financial interest could influence, or look as if it could influence, your work. The right action is to declare it to your manager as soon as you notice it, so that someone else can decide. Smaller matters include using the printer for private documents or taking stationery home. They are small, but they are still misuse. Worked example: you are on a panel assessing quotes from suppliers and you realise that your cousin owns one of the firms. The best response is to tell your manager before the panel takes place, so that you can step back. Keeping quiet is a breach of integrity even if you would be fair. Accepting gifts and hospitality has to be declared and often refused. Ask yourself how your action would look if it were reported in the news.

questions.prompt: You are on a panel assessing supplier quotes and you realise your cousin owns one of the firms. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Stay on the panel but make sure you score your cousin's firm fairly and openly
Say nothing, since you will be honest
Tell your manager before the panel meets so that you can step back
Ask your cousin to withdraw their quote

questions.hint: Declaring the interest lets someone else decide and keeps the process fair.

questions.prompt: You want to print 40 pages of a personal document at work. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Print it, as the cost is small
Print it after hours when nobody else in the office is likely to notice
Print it at home or at a print shop, not on official equipment
Ask a colleague to print it for you

questions.hint: Official resources are for official use.

questions.prompt: A supplier invites you to an expensive lunch while a contract decision is pending. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Decline politely and tell your manager about the invitation
Accept, as long as you pay for your own drink and declare nothing at all
Accept and decide fairly anyway
Accept, but tell the supplier it is a one-off

questions.hint: Hospitality during a decision may look like influence and should be declined and reported.

questions.prompt: A friend asks you to recommend them for a temporary role in your team, though you know they are not the best candidate. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Recommend them to a manager as a favour
Pass them the interview questions
Explain that recruitment is by fair and open competition and suggest they apply
Tell them to use your name in the application

questions.hint: Civil Service appointments are made on merit through fair and open competition.

questions.prompt: You find an error in your favour on an expenses payment of £50. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Tell finance and arrange to repay it
Keep it, because the department made the mistake
Spend it and hope no one checks
Give it to charity quietly

questions.hint: Repaying an overpayment is honest, whatever the amount.

questions.prompt: Your manager asks you to book a flight in business class for a short trip when economy is available and cheaper. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Book it, since your manager asked
Book economy and not tell your manager
Check the travel policy and raise the cost with your manager if it does not fit
Book business class and pay the difference yourself without telling anyone in the department

questions.hint: Following travel policy protects public money.

questions.prompt: A relative is applying for a benefit that your team decides. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Process the application quickly to help them
Process it as normal and say nothing
Ask a friend to process it for you
Tell your manager and make sure you are not involved in the decision

questions.hint: Declaring the link and stepping back keeps the decision fair.

questions.prompt: You are given a free ticket to a concert by a charity your department funds. What is the most effective response?

options.text: Decline the ticket and let your manager know about the offer
Accept, as it is from a charity
Accept it and share it with your team
Accept it and give it to a friend

questions.hint: Gifts from bodies you deal with may look like influence.
